text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- An earthquake that shook Zagreb on Wednesday night was a "strong" one, seizmologists say but predict no further tremors.
- Only half of some 326 Croatian Serb families now living in Ilok, Tovarnik and Vukovar in Eastern Slavonia wish to return to their own homes elswhere in Croatia, says government office for refugees.
- President Tudjman forms a committee for eastablishing constitutional order in Eastern Slavonia and appoints minister of reconstruction and development Jure Radic to chair it.
- Oil company INA may introduce credit cards to be used at its filling stations across the country by the summer, says director of INA-card project Stanko Palaversa.
- Bosnian president Alija Izetbegovic postpones a planned May 5 meeting with his Croatian counterpart Franjo Tudjman by two weeks for health reasons. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
